candidates.title: The Hidden Science of Electron Beam Gun Power Supply
candidates.notes: Qualitative overview only. No efficiency percentages or quantitative data. Discusses switch-mode designs in general terms ('minimal energy loss') but provides no metrics.

candidates.title: E-Beam Power Supplies — Ferrotec
candidates.notes: Accessible, but systems top out at 12 kW (CV-12SLX). No wall-plug efficiency data published. Scale is orders of magnitude below 78 MW requirement.

candidates.title: EB Welding Large Chamber Systems — Sciaky
candidates.notes: Sciaky systems are 42–60 kW beam power for EB welding. MW-scale systems not offered in catalog. No efficiency data accessible. Scale mismatch.

candidates.title: Design of High Efficiency High Power Electron Accelerator Systems Based on Normal Conducting RF Technology — Dolgashev & Tantawi, SLAC, 2018
candidates.notes: MW-scale beam power systems; quantitative efficiency data given (rf-to-beam 79.6%, 96.7%, 97.2% for three linac configurations). However, this is RF accelerator technology, not DC electron guns. Polywell design calls for 'commercial-grade MW-class electron beam injectors' (DC guns), making direct applicability limited. PDF accessible at osti.gov/servlets/purl/1441166 but content is binary-encoded and unreadable via WebFetch.

candidates.title: Electron Beam Melting Furnace — ALD Vacuum Technologies
candidates.notes: Accessible page. ALD offers EB guns up to 800 kW (three tiers: 60 kW, 300 kW, 800 kW). Reports 'power transfer efficiency into the material ranges from approx. 50 to 80%' — this is beam-to-material coupling efficiency, not power supply wall-plug efficiency. No AC-to-beam conversion efficiency stated. Scale approaches MW range but does not reach 78 MW aggregate.

candidates.title: All Solid State High Voltage Power Supply for Neutral Beam Sources — Praeg, ANL, 1984
candidates.notes: Neutral beam (not electron beam) application. No quantitative efficiency data in abstract. Outdated (1984). Not applicable.

candidates.title: Design of 120 MW Beam Power Electron Gun for High Power Klystron — Zhou & Dong, 2005
candidates.notes: Electron gun for klystron microwave generation — fundamentally different application. Abstract accessible via IAEA INIS; full text not accessible. No efficiency data in abstract.

failed.reason: PDF content unreadable via WebFetch (binary-encoded, 8.8 MB). Could not verify whether DC electron gun efficiency data appears in body text. Technology (RF linac) is also not directly applicable to Polywell's DC injection guns.

entries.notes: The commercial industrial EB power supply market operates at 3–800 kW per gun, far below the ~78 MW aggregate injection power described in Park 2025 (which would require many guns or specialized high-power systems not reflected in standard catalog products). No publicly accessible source was found that states wall-plug or AC-to-beam conversion efficiency for DC electron guns at kW-to-MW scale with quantitative data. The analysis estimate of 80–90% efficiency is consistent with general switch-mode power supply performance (IGBT-based inverter designs of this class typically achieve 85–95%), but no citable primary source was identified. Future iterations should try: (1) contacting Leybold, Sciaky, or ALD directly for technical datasheets; (2) searching accelerator physics literature (IPAC proceedings) for electron gun power supply efficiency benchmarks; (3) looking for IAEA TECDOC publications on industrial electron accelerator applications.
